items.title: [FDD Diary #7] I Wrote a Spec. So What.
content:
I can't read code.
So I wrote a spec instead.
Fifteen pages. Purpose, method, structure.
Threw it at Claude.

Three straight days of explosions.

Day one: build timeout.
Day two: code collision.
Day three: a working feature died.

The spec said what to build.
Didn't say what would break.
Couldn't have. Nothing had broken yet.

Made a PROBLEMS.md.
Wrote down every hit.
The pattern emerged.

A spec you write once and never touch?
That's a wish.

Plans change every time you take a punch.
Writing down the changes.
That's what a plan is.

items.title: [FDD Diary #8] 28 Left Arms
content:
'Make me a left arm.'
AI made one. Didn't remove the old one.
Next day, another. Day after, another.

A week later. Twenty-eight left arms.
Left arms on the legs. On the back.
Nineteen deactivated. Six never discovered.

Asked the AI. 'Why new files every time?'

'Modifying existing files could lose content. For safety, I generated a new version.'

Thirty files is safety?

Implementation is free.
Cleanup costs money.
Yesterday's Claude did the work.
Today's GPT does archaeology.

One spec file. One config file.
One document that says 'this is correct.'

Thirty files, thirty stories. Rules collapse.
One file, one story. Rules hold.

SSOT. Single Source of Truth.

items.title: [FDD Diary #9] The Blind Genius
content:
AI is a genius with no eyes.

Three eggs in the fridge.
No shopping list. Buy three more.
Come home to six.

AI isn't dumb.
There's no shopping list.

Had the AI scan every file. Catalog what exists.
Five minutes.

'Build this.' AI checks first.
'Something similar already exists. Modify it?'

Never heard that before.
Because the AI didn't know what was there.

With docs: genius.
Without docs: blind genius.

Update the list every day.
One source of truth.
Got it.

But all of this. Me opening the spec.
Me fixing it. Me saying 'read this first.'

Every. Single. Time.

My hands were the automation.
